problems.quote: The 2015 ordinance on the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC) was challenged on these grounds, though the matter was later rendered academic by the Court’s striking down of the NJAC Act i
problems.problem: There was no 2015 ordinance on the NJAC; the NJAC was established by the Constitution (99th Amendment) Act, 2014 and the NJAC Act, 2014. The Supreme Court struck down both in 2015.
problems.correction: The NJAC was created by a 2014 constitutional amendment and Act, not a 2015 ordinance; the Court struck them down in 2015.
problems.verifierReason: NJAC established by Constitution (99th Amendment) Act, 2014 and NJAC Act, 2014 — no 2015 ordinance existed. Correction accurate.

problems.quote: The 2020 pandemic saw the creation of a high‑level Group of Ministers on COVID‑19, which met daily and reported to the CCS, illustrating the flexibility of the committee system in crisis management.
problems.problem: The Group of Ministers on COVID‑19 reported to the Prime Minister, not to the Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS).
problems.correction: The 2020 pandemic saw the creation of a high‑level Group of Ministers on COVID‑19, which met daily and reported to the Prime Minister.
problems.verifierReason: The COVID-19 Group of Ministers reported to the Prime Minister, not the CCS. Correction accurately fixes the reporting line.

problems.quote: The Supreme Court in R.C. Cooper v. Union of India (1970) held that the President's power to withhold assent is subject to judicial review only on the ground of mala fides or constitutional violation,
problems.problem: R.C. Cooper v. Union of India (1970) dealt with bank nationalisation, not the President's assent power. The relevant case on judicial review of presidential assent is Purushothaman Nambudiri v. State of Kerala (1962).
problems.correction: The Supreme Court in Purushothaman Nambudiri v. State of Kerala (1962) held that the President's power to withhold assent is subject to judicial review only on grounds of mala fides or constitutional
problems.verifierReason: R.C. Cooper (1970) was the Bank Nationalisation case; judicial review of presidential assent was addressed in Purushothaman Nambudiri (1962). Correction accurate.

problems.quote: In a 2017 ruling (primarily on defamation), the Court reiterated that parliamentary privilege cannot override the constitutional guarantee of free speech unless the publication constitutes a clear and
problems.problem: No 2017 Supreme Court ruling on defamation applied a 'clear and present danger' test to parliamentary privilege; that test is not part of Indian parliamentary privilege jurisprudence.
problems.correction: The Supreme Court has not adopted a 'clear and present danger' standard for parliamentary privilege; judicial review is limited to mala fide, excess of jurisdiction, or violation of natural justice.
problems.verifierReason: Original misstates law; 'clear and present danger' not Indian test; correction accurate per Raja Ram Pal.

problems.quote: An amendment to the Rules of Procedure introduced a “cooling‑off” period before a privilege motion can be taken up, aimed at reducing politically motivated notices.
problems.problem: No such amendment has been enacted in the Rules of Procedure of either House; the existing rules require notice before 10 AM on the day of the motion without a cooling-off period.
problems.correction: No amendment has introduced a cooling-off period; notice must be given before 10 AM on the day the privilege motion is to be raised.
problems.verifierReason: No cooling-off period in Rules; notice required before 10 AM same day; correction accurate.

problems.quote: Every two years India submits a Domestic Support Notification (DSN) to the WTO Committee on Agriculture.
problems.problem: WTO Agreement on Agriculture requires annual domestic support notifications, not biennial.
problems.correction: Every year India submits a Domestic Support Notification (DSN) to the WTO Committee on Agriculture.
problems.verifierReason: WTO Agreement on Agriculture requires annual domestic support notifications; biennial is incorrect.

problems.quote: The 2021 Model Agricultural Produce and Livestock Marketing (APLM) Act encourages states to harmonise licensing, enable private market yards, and integrate with the National Agriculture Market (e‑NAM)
problems.problem: The Model APLM Act was released in 2017, not 2021.
problems.correction: The 2017 Model Agricultural Produce and Livestock Marketing (APLM) Act encourages states to harmonise licensing, enable private market yards, and integrate with the National Agriculture Market (e‑NAM)
problems.verifierReason: Model APLM Act was released in 2017, not 2021.

problems.quote: In 2022, the LRF projected "above normal" rainfall (106 % LPA).
problems.problem: The April 2022 Long-Range Forecast (LRF) projected 99% LPA (normal); the June updated forecast projected 103% LPA.
problems.correction: In 2022, the LRF projected "normal" rainfall (99 % LPA).
problems.verifierReason: April 2022 LRF projected 99% LPA (normal); 106% is incorrect.

problems.quote: The strategic reserve norm, revised in 2015, is 5 million tonnes of wheat and 3 million tonnes of rice, over and above the operational requirement of 21 million tonnes (wheat) and 13 million tonnes (r
problems.problem: The 2015 buffer norms set total minimum stocks at ~21 mt wheat and ~13.5 mt rice; the strategic reserve (5 mt wheat, 3 mt rice) is a component of this total, not additional to it.
problems.correction: The strategic reserve norm, revised in 2015, is 5 million tonnes of wheat and 3 million tonnes of rice, included within the total buffer norm of 21 million tonnes (wheat) and 13 million tonnes (rice)
problems.verifierReason: 2015 buffer norms set total minimum stocks at 21 mt wheat and 13.5 mt rice including strategic reserve, not additional.

problems.quote: The release order specifies quantity, destination depots, and the subsidised issue price (typically 50 % of MSP for PDS, 75 % for open‑market sales).
problems.problem: PDS issue prices are fixed at Rs. 2/kg wheat and Rs. 3/kg rice under NFSA (far below 50% of MSP); open-market sales under OMSS use reserve prices, not a fixed 75% of MSP.
problems.correction: The release order specifies quantity, destination depots, and the subsidised issue price (typically Rs. 2/kg for wheat and Rs. 3/kg for rice under NFSA, and reserve prices for open-market sales).
problems.verifierReason: NFSA fixes PDS issue prices at ₹2/kg wheat and ₹3/kg rice; OMSS uses reserve prices, not fixed % of MSP.

problems.quote: In 2022‑23, Punjab’s bonus outlay for wheat and paddy amounted to approximately ₹4,200 crore, representing roughly 1.2 % of the state’s gross fiscal deficit.
problems.problem: Punjab's gross fiscal deficit in 2022-23 was ~₹49,500 crore; ₹4,200 crore is ~8.5% of that deficit, not 1.2%.
problems.correction: In 2022‑23, Punjab’s bonus outlay for wheat and paddy amounted to approximately ₹4,200 crore, representing roughly 8.5 % of the state’s gross fiscal deficit.
problems.verifierReason: Punjab's 2022-23 gross fiscal deficit ~₹49,500 cr; ₹4,200 cr bonus is ~8.5%, not 1.2%.

problems.quote: The FC’s performance‑based incentive for states achieving Sustainable Development Goals targets adds a conditional layer to devolution.
problems.problem: The Finance Commission does not have a performance-based incentive for SDG targets as a conditional layer to devolution; devolution is formula-based, and the 15th FC introduced demographic performance criteria, not SDG-target incentives.
problems.correction: The FC’s devolution formula includes demographic performance criteria, not SDG-target incentives.
problems.verifierReason: 15th FC devolution formula uses demographic performance, not SDG-target incentives; devolution is formula-based.

problems.quote: The state's Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme, launched in 2009
problems.problem: The Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme was launched in 2012; the 2009 scheme was the Kalaignar Kapitu Thittam.
problems.correction: The state's Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme, launched in 2012
problems.verifierReason: CMCHIS launched in 2012; 2009 scheme was Kalaignar Kapitu Thittam.

problems.quote: The 15th Finance Commission's recommendation to link a portion of CSS grants to evaluation compliance remains unimplemented.
problems.problem: The 15th Finance Commission did not recommend linking CSS grants to evaluation compliance; it recommended performance-based sectoral grants and stronger evaluation capacity.
problems.correction: The 15th Finance Commission recommended performance-based sectoral grants and stronger evaluation, but not linking CSS grants to evaluation compliance.
problems.verifierReason: 15th FC recommended performance-based sectoral grants and stronger evaluation, not linking CSS grants to evaluation compliance.

problems.problem: Wrong ministry; the C&D Waste Management Rules, 2016 were issued by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), not MoHUA.
problems.correction: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) issued the “Construction and Demolition (C&D) Waste Management Rules” (2016)
problems.verifierReason: C&D Waste Rules 2016 notified by MoEFCC under Environment (Protection) Act, not MoHUA

problems.quote: amended in 2022 to include a “Disaster Debris Module”
